question: Parenteral nutrition can be defined as:

options.text: removal of excessive food by syringes
infusing a specialised form of food through a vein (intravenously)
infusing a specialised form of food through oral route
intake of glucose and salts through oral route

solution:
The correct answer is, **'infusing a specialized form of food through a vein (intravenously)'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Parental nutrition** is the process in which **nutrition is delivered through veins.**

 
 
• It is used when a person is **unable to get nutrients through intestinal tracts** which can be the result of continuous vomiting, diarrhea, or some other intestinal disease.
 
• There are **4 kinds of Parental routes:**
 
 
• **Intravenous (in a vein)**
 
• **Intramuscular (in a muscle)**
 
• **Intrathecal (around the spinal cord)**
 
• **Subcutaneous (under the skin)**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Removal of excessive food by syringes** is known as** Paracentesis.**
 
• **Infusing a specialized form of food through the oral route** is known as **Enteral Administration.**
 
• **Intake of glucose and salts through the oral route** is known as **Oral Rehydration Therapy**.
